title: Choose the product page structure
question: Three structures for the Casify product page, all in the candy-shop world you already have. Lock one to build, steer one, or re-roll.

options.label: The Order Slip
options.thesis: Buying a case is filling in a candy-shop order slip: phone, style, how many, then the till.
options.viewport: Product photos in a scalloped shop-window frame on the left; a tall paper order slip on the right with lines 1 Your phone, 2 Style, 3 How many, and the red candy button with the live total at its foot.
options.risk: A slip can feel slower than a one-tap buy box unless each line collapses to its answer once chosen.

options.label: The Shop Counter
options.thesis: The familiar two-column product page, built as a candy counter where every control is a counter object.
options.viewport: Sticky photo stage on the left with jar-lid thumbnails; on the right the title, a hanging brass price tag, style swatches, a model picker, three pack boxes, the candy button and a ribbon of service promises.
options.risk: Closest to every Shopify product page; the world has to live in the details or it reads as a template.

options.label: Weigh & Pay
options.thesis: The pack deal is the show: a brass candy scale where adding cases tips the pan and the price per case drops.
options.viewport: Photos top-left, model and style pickers top-right; beneath them a wide brass scale holding 1, 2 and 3 case bags, the chosen bag weighed down with its per-case price, and the add button on a chalkboard card.
options.risk: Puts pack value ahead of fit; a visitor who wants one case can feel upsold.
